mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over a 3-month window signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when the trigger is met, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered months, or the median return is not significantly negative at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which elevates input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month simultaneously signals a broad-based demand shock, which depresses earnings and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 m/m change < -1% AND HOUST m/m change < -1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of co-triggered months, or the joint signal does not produce a statistically significant negative return at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid reduction in the federal funds rate below 2% during a recessionary regime signals an aggressive easing cycle, which lowers discount rates and supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of co-triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly above zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals persistent labor market weakness, which reduces consumer demand and corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered periods, or the average return is not significantly below zero at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal savings (implied by RSAFS decline) combined with a rise in the consumer price index above 3% for three consecutive months signals inflationary pressure with constrained real income, which erodes purchasing power and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3.0% for 3 consecutive months AND RSAFS m/m change < -1% in the same month
regime_hint: inflationary environment with falling real savings
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of co-triggered months, or the joint signal does not yield a statistically significant negative return at the 5% level.
